units.text: Here is a little face on a grid of squares. Count the filled squares in each row, and in each column. Those counts are the picture's two shadows. Hide the picture and keep the shadows. Could a different picture cast the same shadows?

It can. Every row count matches, and every column count matches. They differ in four squares, the corners of a rectangle, with filled and empty corners alternating. Swap filled and empty at those corners. Each of their rows and columns loses one square and gains one. That move is a switch. It changes the picture, but neither shadow.
How many pictures cast these shadows? Sixty-four, and each is at most three switches from the face.

Change the column counts but keep their total, and no picture fits at all. This column needs a square in every row, but the middle row is empty. So shadows raise two questions. Does any picture fit? And is it the only one?
